title: Vice President Vance broke a voting tie to block a Senate bill
description_short: Vice President Vance broke a voting tie to block a Senate bill aiming to curb President Trump's military action in Venezuela
description_medium: On January 15, 2026, Vice President JD Vance cast the tie-breaking Senate vote against a bill aimed at limiting President Trump’s military action in Venezuela. Reports said several Republican senators changed their votes after Trump pressed them. The bill’s text and roll-call record are needed to determine which authority it would have constrained.
description_long: Vice President JD Vance cast the tie-breaking Senate vote on January 15, 2026, blocking a measure aimed at limiting President Donald Trump’s military action in Venezuela. Several Republican senators who had initially supported the bill changed their votes after Trump pressured them. Vance’s vote decided a close result in a chamber divided over the administration’s use of force. The event record does not identify the bill number or reproduce its text, so the exact authority it sought to restrict is unclear. Without the measure’s language and the Senate roll call, it is not possible to determine which military action or legal power the bill addressed. The vote shows Congress considered a limit on presidential action in Venezuela, but the scope and effect of that proposal need the official bill and vote record.

title: The United States carries out three strikes on four suspected drug trafficking
description_short: The United States carries out three strikes on four suspected drug trafficking vessels in the Pacific ocean killing fourteen and wounding one
description_medium: On October 27, 2025, the U.S. military carried out three strikes on four suspected drug-trafficking vessels in the eastern Pacific. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth said 14 people were killed and one survivor was transferred to Mexican authorities for rescue. The administration did not publicly identify the vessels or provide details of the alleged cargo.
description_long: The U.S. military carried out three strikes on four vessels in the eastern Pacific on October 27, 2025. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth described the boats as operated by designated terrorist organizations and said the strikes killed 14 people; one person survived and was turned over to Mexican authorities for rescue. The administration did not identify the vessels’ origins or publicly provide details about the narcotics they were alleged to carry. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum objected to the attacks and called for international treaties to be respected. The strikes formed part of a broader campaign against boats the administration accused of drug trafficking. The stated accusation does not establish that the targets were carrying drugs or that those killed belonged to a designated group. The operation raised questions about the legal basis for lethal force outside a declared battlefield and the evidence used to identify the boats. The event records the strikes, casualties, rescue, and diplomatic objection without treating the administration’s claims about the targets as independently proven.
